newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative Clarke tops consultative poll.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative Clarke tops consultative poll.

text.p: Former finance minister Kenneth Clarke on Tuesday came top of a consultative ballot of Conservative constituency chairmen ahead of the second ballot for the election of the party's leader.
But Clarke's lead over main rival William Hague was narrower than in a similar straw poll ahead of last Tuesday's first ballot.

Sir Archie Hamilton, chairman of the 1922 Committee of Conservative backbench MPs, which is organising the leadership election, said Clarke won the votes of 242 constituency chairmen from England, Wales and Northern Ireland against 223 for Hague.
Euro-sceptic former cabinet minister John Redwood trailed with 28 votes.
Clarke won the votes of 152 Conservative peers against 59 for Hague and 20 for Redwood.
Scottish constituency chairmen split 44 for Clarke, 15 for Hague and two for Redwood.
The executive of the National Union, the Conservatives' voluntary arm, voted 88 for Clarke, 70 for Hague and 16 for Redwood.
All 17 Conservative MEPs backed Clarke, a pro-European.
The ballot is completely non-binding on the 164 Conservative MPs who started voting at 0900 GMT on a successor to John Major.
If, as expected, there is no outright winner when the result of the vote is announced around 1620 GMT, the two front-runners will square off on Thursday.
Clarke enjoyed a clearer lead in last week's consultative ballot, when he had a 91-vote margin over Hague in the poll of English chairmen and a 47-vote lead among National Union members.
